newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo Brazzaville council extends Lissouba mandate.
newsitem.headline: Congo Brazzaville council extends Lissouba mandate.

text.p: The embattled Congo Republic's Constitutional Council has formally postponed a July 27 presidential election and extended President Pascal Lissouba's mandate until polling can be held, diplomats said on Monday.

The council, meeting across the river in the capital Brazzaville at the weekend, agreed the move as envoys from Lissouba and his predecessor Denis Sassou Nguesso held talks in Gabon on a lasting end to bloody political and ethnic fighting.
A fragile ceasefire, which took effect in Brazzaville on July 14, has more or less held -- making it the longest truce since the fighting began on June 5.
It was not immediately clear whether the prolongation of Lissouba's mandate would be limited to a 90-day period set out in the constitution.
"It looks as if the council didn't get too hung up about the 90-day business," one political analyst commented. "The decision is like waving a red cloth under Sassou's nose."
Sassou has been demanding a government of national salvation to run the oil-producing former French colony until elections.
Lissouba's mandate expires at the end of August.
The rival delegations in Gabon's capital Libreville have yet to meet face-to-face.
Gabon's President Omar Bongo and fellow international mediator Mohamed Shanoun, U.N. and Organisation of African Unity special envoy on the crisis, have met each side separately.
They were due to meet Sassou's delegation on Monday, U.N. officials said.

"We hope to find our way onto the path of negotiations between the Congolese themselves," Sahnoun told Radio France International at the weekend. "The Congolese people are getting fed up. They no longer want this fratricidal war.''
No heavy weapons have been fired in Brazzaville since Wednesday evening when there were signs of a reconciliation between Sassou and Lissouba loyalists.
The showdown began after government troops surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militia ahead of the July 27 election.
Medical workers say hundreds of people have died, many of them civilians killed by indiscriminate shelling.
Plans for a U.N. sponsored, mainly African peacekeeping force are taking shape. Senegal has agreed to command it.
